providers.surface: Claude Code OAuth live five-hour and weekly usage windows
providers.selectedSource: Preferred OAuth GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage using the current native Claude Code session; optional same-token GET /api/oauth/profile
providers.sourceStatusReason: Unofficial WATCH source: Token Jar uses the CodexBar-style preferred OAuth GET path plus bounded automatic Claude Code owner renewal, not CodexBar's fallback chain. Only claudeAiOauth is eligible; MCP is never accepted or renewed. Only a successful live response is fresh. Token Jar never POSTs, writes, copies, directly refreshes, or caches a Claude token; Claude Code owns rotation and its official .oauth_refresh.lock.
providers.credentialPersistence: Claude-owned ~/.claude/.credentials.json and native Keychain generic-password service Claude Code-credentials with account NSUserName(); Token Jar performs exact read-only access and keeps no Claude credential cache, while Claude Code alone may rotate its stores under .oauth_refresh.lock
tokenTankIO: Read claudeAiOauth only from ~/.claude/.credentials.json and the native generic-password service Claude Code-credentials with account NSUserName(); never match another same-service account. Require user:profile, finite positive expiry more than 60 seconds away, and a token not known to have received usage HTTP 401. MCP tokens are never accepted or renewed

On near expiry or usage HTTP 401, reread both exact slots. Retain rejected-token identity independently per file/Keychain slot (at most two), even after adopting the other store's fresh token, preventing A/B oscillation. If both slots are rejected, the next eligible 401 forces single-flight owner renewal

GET only https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage and optionally same-token /api/oauth/profile. Retry usage at most once and only with a changed token. HTTP 403 never renews; 429 observes backoff. Network, timeout, schema, authentication, and recovery failures retain prior in-memory data only as stale, never fresh

allowInteraction controls native Keychain UI only and is preserved for initial, pre-renewal, and post-renewal reads. Background reads and reloads are noninteractive; user-initiated reads may allow native UI. Calls remain serialized and bounded at 5 seconds background/120 seconds interactive, skip locked/off-console native access, reject unresolved overlap, and discard late results

SecKeychainGet/SetUserInteractionAllowed changes only Token Jar's process-local policy and is restored on every exit. It does not modify ACLs or user settings and cannot guarantee that an independent Claude Code or security child never displays macOS authorization UI

Automatic owner renewal launches only unlocked/on-console using fixed absolute Claude candidates, an empty mode-0700 workspace, minimal fixed environment, and fixed safe-mode/no-tools arguments. Prompt veto precedes readiness and success; confirm only the exact trust question in the verified-empty workspace and never after /usage

Require readiness banner plus shift+tab before exactly /usage, then a completed panel plus one second quiet; loading/tab headers do not complete. Completed flow sends Esc then /exit with five-second grace. Hard deadline after /usage waits passively five seconds without input before termination; pre-readiness deadline cleans up immediately without input
A failed token enters a token-keyed 300-second background cooldown; still reread credentials first, adopt a fresh external token immediately, and allow explicit manual refresh to bypass the cooldown

Do not import browser cookies, scrape PTY usage, automate login/browser approval, call Admin or inference APIs, use ~/.claude.json cached usage, or directly POST/write/copy/cache a Claude token. Missing or revoked login requires claude auth login; web or Claude Desktop login is not a substitute
externalPaths: native Keychain generic-password service Claude Code-credentials; account NSUserName() only
providers.tccClass: none; allowInteraction permits only user-initiated native Keychain UI. Background native reads and reloads are noninteractive, but the process-local setting cannot guarantee suppression in an independent Claude Code or security child
providers.liveValidation: 2026-09-12 local verification: package 194 tests/12 suites passed three consecutive runs; app 35 and bilingual Claude recovery UI 1 passed against final source; unsigned universal arm64+x86_64 Release rebuilt. An earlier unrelated Codex one-second test timeout passed isolated reproduction and the next three whole suites without Codex changes. Provider I/O audit and manifest/localization validation passed. Independent Grok implementation review approved the session, owner runner, adapter and native/PTY tests with no findings. The final production runner rejected the login-required marker without further input; natural-expiry and real-401 authenticated rotation remain unverified. No installation/deployment occurred; intentional legacy Keychain deprecation warnings remain.
providers.mutationRisk: Token Jar performs no Claude token POST/write/copy/cache. Rejected memory is per source slot (at most two), preventing A/B oscillation. Prompt veto precedes readiness/success and trust never follows /usage. Completed flow gets Esc and /exit grace; post-usage hard deadline is passive and pre-readiness deadline supplies no input. Claude Code alone owns rotation and .oauth_refresh.lock.
providers.releaseBlocker: WATCH: verify the new automatic recovery implementation, including natural near-expiry and real HTTP 401 changed-token recovery, exact-account Keychain adoption behind a rejected file token, 403 no-renewal, cooldown/single-flight behavior, and final candidate security and release gates. Historical v1-v4 and clean 489ba51 artifacts are not publishable.

providers.selectedSource: Grok-owned ~/.grok/auth.json OIDC session; when access expiry is within 60 seconds or the first credits proxy request returns 401/403, refresh_token grant at fixed https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/token and atomic same-file rotation, then one proxy retry; primary cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits; only when a successful proxy response leaves usage unknown, bearer-only POST https://grok.com/grok_api_v2.GrokBuildBilling/GetGrokCreditsConfig with the same session bearer and a 6-second timeout
providers.sourceStatusReason: The Grok CLI owner session and CLI-proxy credits endpoint remain primary. Unlike CodexBar, which is only a reference for credits behavior and does not directly refresh OAuth, Token Jar performs the user-approved narrow renewal: an OIDC access token expiring within 60 seconds, or one rejected by the first proxy request with 401/403, is renewed once through the official fixed token endpoint after exact issuer and selected client/scope checks; the rotated session is atomically preserved to the same owner file before one proxy retry. Only a successful proxy snapshot with unknown usage may trigger the existing same-session bearer-only gRPC-web billing fallback. Proxy reset, source metadata, and account identity remain authoritative; web billing supplies usage only. Token Jar never imports browser cookies, uses Grok ACP stdio or a CLI subprocess, offers manual-token UI, calls the xAI Management prepaid-balance API, or caches tokens in Keychain.
providers.rejectedAlternative: Browser-cookie imports, Grok ACP stdio, CLI subprocess or interactive automation, manual-token UI, local-session estimates, xAI Management API/prepaid-balance calls, Keychain token caches, backups, other secret stores, and arbitrary credential copying remain prohibited. The older Grok Build ACP x.ai/billing probe returned JSON-RPC -32601 (method-not-found) on official Grok 1.0.13.
providers.credentialOwner: Grok CLI, with user-approved Token Jar renewal of the selected OIDC entry
providers.credentialPersistence: Grok-owned ~/.grok/auth.json; Token Jar may atomically replace only that same file after a successful official refresh_token grant, preserving the optional rotated refresh token and updated expires_at; no backup, copy, or other secret store
tokenTankIO: Open only ~/.grok/auth.json through the Grok-scoped session capability; require issuer https://auth.x.ai and exact agreement between the selected client/scope suffix and the entry's non-empty oidc_client_id

When expires_at is within 60 seconds, or only after the first credits proxy request returns 401/403, POST a refresh_token grant to fixed https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/token with public-client authentication, no cookies, and no redirects

Once renewal starts, hold a bounded token-free lock shared only by Token Jar processes across reread, rotation, comparison, and persistence. Install the cancellation handler before checking cancellation so cancellation before waiter registration still seals the waiter gate. A started transaction settles before a canceled observer receives CancellationError; pre-start cancellation aborts
HTTPS GET https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits with the selected ephemeral bearer; after 401/403 renewal, retry this proxy exactly once

Only when a successful proxy response leaves usage unknown, POST https://grok.com/grok_api_v2.GrokBuildBilling/GetGrokCreditsConfig with the same selected bearer, a 5-byte empty gRPC-web data frame (00 00 00 00 00), no cookies, and a 6-second timeout

Preserve proxy reset, source metadata, and account identity; adopt a published web percentage, or an omitted proto3 scalar as zero only for a structurally complete response with a recognized current weekly/monthly period containing the refresh time; otherwise retain unknown, including a failed fallback
Expose published creditUsagePercent or the same-row on-demand used/cap ratio under the credits quota
Display only the selected auth entry's optional email in memory; never infer identity from another entry or token
providers.liveValidation: Historical Grok renewal/usage evidence remains scoped to its original revision. After the cancellation repair, package 172/12 passed three consecutive runs and app 35/full UI 19 reran and passed. Repair-commit CI remains pending.
providers.mutationRisk: The only credential mutation allowed is successful Grok renewal written atomically to the same ~/.grok/auth.json through a same-directory mode-0600 temporary file. A bounded token-free lock covers reread, HTTP rotation, comparison, and persistence among Token Jar processes; once renewal starts it settles despite observer cancellation, after which a canceled observer receives CancellationError after commit, while pre-start cancellation aborts. Comparison detects observable external rotation and prefers a newer session but cannot close the final rename window against an uncooperative concurrent Grok CLI writer; the lock is not claimed to be CLI-honored. No backup, other secret store, cookie import, Management API fallback, or unrelated source-store mutation is allowed.
providers.releaseBlocker: WATCH: live-validate a naturally near-expiry event, real proxy HTTP 401/403 renewal, concurrent real Grok CLI rotation, missing/revoked versus network-error recovery, and the packaged final candidate on supported OS versions; complete CI, signing, and notarization evidence

Token Jar follows the current CodexBar behavior as a reference, reads the Cursor-owned SQLite value in place with immutable=1 and no persistence or refresh, and fails closed on expiry or schema drift.

tokenTankIO: Open only Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb with O_NOFOLLOW, verify the opened descriptor identity, bind immutable=1 SQLite to that descriptor, and query only ItemTable cursorAuth/accessToken and cursorAuth/cachedEmail
Require a canonical token envelope, bounded allowed subject, and unexpired timestamp; use it only in an ephemeral owner-session cookie whose authority is decided by cursor.com/api/usage-summary
Expose individual and team usage blocks, plan breakdowns, and percentages independently with opaque identities
Display optional cachedEmail from the same SQLite read in memory only; absent or invalid email does not suppress usage
providers.liveValidation: Immutable exact-key read preserved all tracked main/WAL/SHM facts and the owner session returned the expected usage-summary root and individual plan/onDemand blocks; ordinary mode=ro was rejected after it changed SQLite metadata.
providers.mutationRisk: Immutable SQLite ignores active WAL state rather than touching shared-memory metadata; an older/expired checkpointed token fails closed. No browser import, token cache, copy, refresh, or external-store mutation is allowed.
providers.releaseBlocker: Revalidate the descriptor-bound immutable read, sanitized schema, and exact owner path through the final frozen candidate
